newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria Jan-Sept trade swings to $2.2 bln surplus.
newsitem.headline: Algeria Jan-Sept trade swings to $2.2 bln surplus.

text.p: Algeria's trade for the first nine months of this year produced a surplus of $2.2 billion against a deficit of $1.1 billion over the same period a year ago, the cabinet said on Tuesday.
In a report of the meeting carried by the official news agency APS, Trade Minister Bakhti Belaid said oil and gas exports totalled $8.49 billion against $6.76 billion for the same period last year.
Hydrocarbon sales abroad, mainly oil and gas, made up 94.4 percent of the North African OPEC member country's exports.
Imports in the first three quarters of this year fell 19 percent, to $6.6 billion from $8.2 billion, the agency reported him telling the cabinet.
The fall in imports was mainly in food, raw and semi-finished materials and items such as medicines, spare parts and tyres, the agency quoted the minister as saying.
Food imports fell overall by eight percent, with cereals, flour and semolina dropping six percent, sugar and sugar products 30 percent, and milk and milk products 31 percent.
Raw and semi-finished imports fell 36 percent, while medicine imports dropped 29 percent, it said.
Algeria spent $2.33 billion on farming and industrial equipment imports in January-September, up eight percent compared from the same period in 1995.
Some 85.4 percent of Algeria's imports and 87.6 percent of its exports were with OECD countries, and the European Union took 65 percent of all exports and provided 59.6 percent of imports.
The minister said the main recipients of Algeria's exports were Italy (22.4 percent), United States (14.7 percent), France (12.35 percent), Spain (8.1 percent) and the Netherlands (7.15 percent).
Countries exporting to Algeria were France (25.1 percent), Spain (12.5 percent), United States (9.7 percent), Italy (9.35 percent), Germany (7.3 percent) and Canada (4.35 percent).
Algeria had its largest trade surplus with Italy, a $1.39 billion surplus, the agency quoted the minister as saying.
Italy is a major consumer of Algerian gas -- some 24 billion cubic metres a year -- via a gas pipeline running through Tunisia and the Mediterranean.
Earlier this month Algeria inaugurated a gas pipeline to Spain and Portugal, with an annual capacity of about nine billion cubic metres.
